title: Set the bin size and rough layout

text: Set the bin footprint, then size the pockets before fine-tuning their positions.
Drag each pocket into a rough position. We’ll check the size and gaps next.
Use position and rotation to arrange the tools with room around each pocket.
Round the pocket edges. Adjust clearance after trying the printed fit check.

title: Create the USB cable pocket with Finger access

text: In addition to the photos, we’ll create a pocket for the USB cable using Finger access.
Measure the coiled cable, then set the slot’s width, length, and depth. Calipers help with depth.

title: Measure once and adjust X/Y scale

text: Measure the real tool with calipers. Compare its length, handle width, and head width with the outline.
Keep proportions links width and length. Unlock it when the X and Y corrections differ.
Use your measured dimensions to size the other tools. These values are for this example.
Export a thin fit check now, before committing to the full bin.
Tool outlines uses less material to check the three photographed tools.
Choose Full surface to include the USB cable pocket created with Finger access.
The fit-check files are saved. Print at 100% scale and try the real tools.

title: Try the fit check with the real tools

text: Place the real tools in the printed fit check. Use the fit and your measurements to guide adjustments.
If needed, adjust the contour, size, or clearance and print another fit check.
A thin fit check tests the openings. Measure pocket depth and tool seating separately.

title: Set pocket depths and add finger access

text: Adjust pocket depth based on measurements of each real tool. Use calipers for accurate depth measurements.
Add two more finger-access scoops so the tools are easy to lift out.

title: Color the bin and fix the warning

text: Use a gray body with black pocket floors and a black rim.
The black floor layer reaches the recesses between the base feet.
Reduce pocket depth from 39 to 38.5 mm to leave more floor underneath.
The warning clears. The tool sits 0.5 mm higher; check that seating depth.
Inspect the rounded edges, pocket floors, cable pocket, and finger scoops.
Cross-section View helps inspect the interior. The exported model remains whole.

title: Export the final bin and preserve the project

text: After the real tools fit and pocket depths are checked, export the full bin.
Save the finished bin and an editable project backup.
Keep the editable project with the print file. Check the slicer preview before printing.
